references.text: Usually, leaven was forbidden in offerings to the Lord, which makes the exception in the thank offering remarkable.
The context of the thank offering (זֶבַח תּוֹדָה) as part of the peace offering, where unleavened bread was also to be brought together with leavened bread.
At the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), two loaves of leavened bread (לֶחֶם חָמֵץ) were to be brought as a firstfruits offering, another case where leavened bread was permitted.
The command not to offer blood together with leavened bread highlights the contrast with the thank offering, where leavened bread was allowed.
Description of grain offerings that were to accompany various types of sacrifices, including peace offerings.
The psalmist mentions paying vows and bringing a thank offering (תּוֹדָה) to God.
An exhortation to offer thank offerings (זִבְחֵי תוֹדָה) and to declare the Lord's deeds with joy.
The prophet Amos mentions thank offerings of leavened bread (חָמֵץ תּוֹדָה) in an ironic context regarding Israel's religious practices.
